headline: Tabled PFAS sewer ordinance; passed capital budget resolutions including $850,000 JFK Coliseum chiller plant; authorized negotiations toward Wilson School property sale.
summary: The meeting included public comment on kratom sales, property revaluations, and parking at the Hartnett lot, plus an audit report. The board chose Donald Spencer over Randy Tremblay for the Ward 7 school board seat; confirmation comes at the next meeting. It also tabled a PFAS sewer ordinance and authorized negotiations for a possible sale of the Wilson School property.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including residential 50/50 sidewalk petitions, Green Streets canopy projects, and the Derryfield School license, except items 7 and 28.
Received and filed the Board of Assessors notice that preliminary revaluation notices were mailed to residential owners.
Tabled the committee's recommendation to pass the PFAS amendment to the sewer ordinance, Chapter 52.
Accepted with regret the resignation of Brian Beaupre from the Planning Board.
Accepted with regret the resignation of Nick Taylor from the Zoning Board.
Accepted with regret the resignation of Christopher Potter from the Board of School Committee.
Chose Donald Spencer over Randy Tremblay for the Ward 7 School Committee seat by roll call, 7 to 5, with one abstention; confirmation vote at next meeting.
Confirmed the Arts Commission and Manchester Housing and Redevelopment Authority appointments as presented.
Confirmed the Planning Board nominees to the Southern New Hampshire Planning Commission, including Alderman O'Neil.
Approved the city's acceptance of the return of 401 Spruce Street from Families in Transition.
Approved an agreement with the Los Angeles Organizing Committee for the Olympic Games 2028 for a torch relay and cauldron lighting in Manchester.
Approved designating the Office of the City Clerk and the Manchester Police Department to issue No Trespass Orders for City property.
Sent the $15,000 opioid and substance use recovery service expansion at 200 Elm Street to the Committee on Finance; motion carried with Alderman Kantor opposed.
Accepted the committee report on $106,697.19 for the Solids Disposal Master Plan and referred it to the Committee on Finance.
Accepted the committee report on $469,567.03 for Secondary Clarifier design and construction and referred it to the Committee on Finance.
Approved the capital budget resolutions, including $850,000 for the JFK Coliseum chiller plant, to pass and be enrolled.
Approved adding one full-time Police Lieutenant position to oversee the Parking Unit.
Approved Water Works staffing changes: eliminating three Accounting Technician II positions and adding one Accountant I and two Customer Service Representative III positions.
Approved limiting Maple Street to a single northbound lane and changing no-parking zones on Maple Street.
Approved no-parking signs in the new Karatzas Heights subdivision off Karatzas Avenue.
Authorized Mayor Ruais to negotiate a possible purchase and sale agreement for the Wilson School property, with Kantor and Sapienza abstaining.
